title: Good Good built the creator economy's dream business. Now it's become its cautionary tale
tldr: A deep dive into how a celebrated creator-led business unraveled, exposing structural weaknesses in creator-economy business models. A rich case study on what happens when creator brands scale past their foundations.
why_fresh: concrete cautionary case study on creator-economy fragility
angle: What the Good Good collapse teaches content strategists about building durable creator brands over hype.

title: Future of TV Briefing: How strong are the fundamentals of the creator economy, really?
tldr: A critical examination of whether the creator economy's underlying economics hold up amid the hype. Useful counter-narrative for anyone building content or influencer strategy.
angle: Is the creator economy overbuilt? What content leaders should stress-test before over-investing.

title: 'Did you use AI?' is the wrong question. Ask 'What did you use AI for?'
tldr: Argues the publishing world's AI panic misframes the debate — process transparency matters more than a binary yes/no. Reframes how comms and content teams should think about disclosure.
angle: Building an AI-use disclosure framework for content teams that focuses on purpose, not presence.

title: Microtrends reshape social media, consumer habits
tldr: Examines how micro-trends are fragmenting social media and shifting consumer content-consumption behavior. Directly relevant to how people consume content today.
angle: How to build content pillars flexible enough to ride microtrends without losing brand coherence.

title: Your Best-Ranked Page Might Be Invisible to Google's AI
tldr: Top-ranked SEO pages may not appear in Google's AI Overviews, breaking the old rules of search visibility. Critical shift for content strategy and discoverability.
angle: Rebuilding content architecture for AI answer engines, not just blue links.

title: On September 15 the Web Starts Hiding From AI, and It Takes Your Press Coverage With It
tldr: A shift in how sites block AI crawlers could make earned press coverage invisible to AI answer engines. Big implications for PR measurement and visibility strategy.
angle: When AI can't see your press, what does earned media even mean? Rethinking PR value in the AI-answer era.

title: Media as a distinctive brand asset
tldr: Argues that media placements themselves — like logos and jingles — can build distinctive brand associations. A fresh lens merging media buying with brand-asset theory.
angle: Treating your owned channels and placements as distinctive brand assets, not just distribution.

title: The AI and Communications Blueprint: 4 Things Every Comms Leader Needs to Get Right
tldr: Outlines what comms leaders must nail for AI adoption to stick — chiefly change management and internal understanding. Practical for internal comms and content governance.
angle: The internal-comms playbook for making AI adoption actually land with skeptical teams.

title: 5 Signs Your Financial Content Program Has a Credibility Problem
tldr: AI engines and buyers now favor named, credentialed experts — anonymous content loses trust. A concrete diagnostic for human-centered, authoritative content.
angle: Why named human experts are becoming your content's biggest trust asset in the AI era.

title: Is AI Making It So Anyone Can Run Effective TikTok Ads?
tldr: TikTok's new AI tools (Agentic Hub, Symphony Creative Studio) lower the barrier to creating and optimizing ad campaigns. Signals democratization of paid social creative.
angle: When AI makes everyone a media buyer, what's left as competitive advantage? Craft and strategy.

title: Mark Ritson: Even the world's best marketers are struggling to find new roles
tldr: Ritson observes a tough job market even for elite marketers, signaling a structural shift in the profession. Relevant for anyone tracking the state of the industry.
why_fresh: contrarian read on marketing job market
angle: What the marketing-talent squeeze says about how the discipline is being restructured by AI and consolidation.

title: Andrew Tindall: Timothy Taylor's rebrand reminds us that time is a marketer's best friend
tldr: Uses a brewery rebrand to argue for consistency and patience over constant reinvention. A grounded brand-building case study against short-termism.
angle: The case for narrative patience: why brand stories compound over years, not campaigns.

title: Good isn't good enough: beware the design middle ground
tldr: Argues design is drifting toward safe mediocrity through an 'accumulation of reasonable decisions.' A sharp critique of homogenized, polish-over-personality creative.
angle: How AI and risk-aversion are pulling content and design to a bland center — and how to resist it.

title: Counter-Print's new book argues merch is making a big comeback
tldr: Makes the case that branded merchandise has re-emerged as a powerful, tangible marketing tool. A physical-content angle amid digital saturation.
why_fresh: reviving physical merch as content channel
angle: Merch as owned media: why tangible brand objects cut through in an AI-flooded feed.
